answer: Mix secret test jobs into paid work: one task in ten has a known answer, indistinguishable from real customer tasks. Every worker locks 100 credits; a wrong test burns the bond, while each completed job pays at most five. A sparrow bot cannot spot the lotus test among ordinary requests, so blind guessing risks ten credits per job to chase five. Keys writing a sonnet instead of doing the work gain nothing. This needs tests that remain secret and representative; a farm that actually solves them pays the real work cost.
